selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the journey described in this passage?
questions.answer: The journey is to see and understand the proofs that show the oneness of Allah.

questions.question: Who is the central figure in the short narrative of the passage?
questions.answer: The central figure is a traveler seeking firm faith.

questions.question: Why did he question everything around him?
questions.answer: He questioned everything to learn about and identify his Creator.

questions.question: How did the traveler search through the cosmos?
questions.answer: He searched with his mind, reflecting on all things and asking what they indicate about the Creator.

questions.question: What invitation does he give to his intellect?
questions.answer: He invites it to join him in another journey to observe the proofs of unity.

questions.question: What does the phrase “let us depart” suggest about the intellect?
questions.answer: It suggests the intellect is an active partner in the journey toward truth.

questions.question: How are those four truths described in relation to the cosmos?
questions.answer: They are described as prevailing over the entire cosmos.

questions.question: What is the significance of the number four in this passage?
questions.answer: It marks the set of major truths they first encounter as proofs of unity.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the traveler trying to understand after becoming sure of Allah’s existence?
questions.answer: He is trying to understand the evidences for Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What kind of person is the traveler presented as being?
questions.answer: He is presented as someone seeking faith with seriousness and purpose.

questions.question: How did he carry out his search across the cosmos?
questions.answer: He carried it out by mentally traveling through the universe and reflecting on all things.

questions.question: What does the passage show about the relationship between the world and knowledge of Allah?
questions.answer: It presents the world as full of signs that help a person know Allah.

questions.question: What does “necessary existence” suggest about Allah in this passage?
questions.answer: It suggests that Allah’s existence is absolute and not dependent on anything else.

questions.question: What new goal does he set before his intellect?
questions.answer: He sets the goal of seeing the proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: What is the first location mentioned in this new journey?
questions.answer: The first location is the first stopping-place.

questions.question: Where do they first stop?
questions.answer: They first stop at the initial station of the new journey.

questions.question: What is the title or subject of this section?
questions.answer: This section is about evidences for Divine unity.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the extent of his mental journey?
questions.answer: It says he traveled through the entire cosmos in thought.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the traveler’s original reason for being sent into the world?
questions.answer: His purpose is to gain true faith.

questions.question: What had the traveler already reached before speaking to his intellect?
questions.answer: He had reached certainty regarding the necessarily existent Creator.

questions.question: What shift happens when he speaks to his intellect?
questions.answer: The search shifts from proving existence to examining unity.

questions.question: At the first stopping-place, what did they encounter?
questions.answer: They encountered four sacred truths spread across the whole universe.

questions.question: What did they witness there?
questions.answer: They witnessed four sacred truths dominating the whole cosmos.

questions.question: What happened when they departed together?
questions.answer: They arrived at the first stopping-place.
